utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] IT-05-86-I, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Trbic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand? If that's the case, please tell us and you can sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please sit down. I'm going to ask for the appearances, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Peter McCloskey and Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the Defence to introduce themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'm Eugene O'Sullivan, appearing for Mr. Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to greet all those who are here in the courtroom; the Prosecutor, Defence counsel, Mr. Milorad Trbic. And I should not forget to greet all those present here in the courtroom; the registrar, the usher, the legal officer, and let's not forget all those who assist us within and outside of this courtroom. Today's hearing is dedicated to the initial appearance of Mr. Milorad Trbic. Let me remind you first that the accused here was transferred to the Detention Unit of the Tribunal on the 7th of April, 2005. Previously, on the 24th of March, 2005, Judge Liu confirmed an indictment established by the Prosecutor and dated 10th of February, 2005, against Pandurevic and against the accused Trbic. Following this indictment that was submitted to the accused, it is stated that at the beginning of the month of July 1995, units of the Drina Corps of the Bosnian Serb army shelled Srebrenica and attacked Dutch-manned United Nations observation posts which were located in the safe area. It is further stated in the indictment that the Bosnian Serb forces entered Srebrenica. It is also stated that between 11th of July, 1995, and 18th of July, 1995, and I quote: "The VRS forces under the command and control of Ratko Mladic, Radoslav Krstic and Vinko Pandurevic either expelled or killed most of the members of the Bosnian Muslim population of the Srebrenica enclave." Milorad Trbic, a security officer in the Zvornik Brigade under the command of Vinko Pandurevic, took part in organising the receipt, detention, and murder of thousands of Bosnian Muslim men transported to the zone of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade from 13 through 17 of July, 1995, and he personally executed in Orahovac Muslim men from Srebrenica during this time period. As a result of these actions, the VRS forces virtually eliminated the presence of any Bosnian Muslims in the Srebrenica enclave area, thus continuing an ethnic cleansing campaign which had begun in the spring of 1992. It is also stated in the indictment that during these events Milorad Trbic was an assistant to Lieutenant Drago Nikolic, who was the chief of security of the Zvornik Brigade, and he reported directly to him. Milorad Trbic held the rank of reserve captain. The accused is charged on the basis of his individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal on a single count, a count of crime against humanity; Article 5 of the Statute, murder. I have just given a brief reminder of the charges against the accused. By an order delivered on 8th of April, 2005, the president of the Tribunal assigned this case to Trial Chamber II, the Trial Chamber I was myself assigned to as a Judge. We had the opportunity to meet once before, on the 13th of April, 2005, and when I asked the accused if he was in a position to react to the indictment, he stated that he wanted to take advantage of the 30-days delay provided for by Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence before entering his plea. This time period of 30 days has now come to an end, and it is now my duty to move on to that phase of the proceedings, and I will in a few minutes ask the accused how he's going to plead. Furthermore, I should state also that on the 20th of April, 2005, I was assigned as Pre-Trial Judge in this case. This being said, Mr. Trbic, I'm now going to ask you to rise, and I'm going to tell you -- to ask you once again to tell me your first name and last name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milorad Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 22nd of February, 1958.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born in the village of Ponijevo, near Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before being transferred to the Detention Unit, what was your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I worked in the USA in a company called Lorenpolo [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In what capacity?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in the field of energy. I graduated from mechanical engineering school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As an accused, you enjoy a number of rights that are listed in Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute. During the last hearing, the registrar read out these rights to you. It is, therefore, not necessary unless you insist, it is not necessary for us to state these rights again, but if you'd like, we can do so. I could ask the registrar to read them out again. Would you like us to read Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute again or do you remember what was read out to you last time?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not necessary to read them out again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Trbic, the Rule provides that the indictment should be read out to you, but you can waive that right if you decide so. Mr. O'Sullivan, what is your position on that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. In the last 30 days I've had a chance to review this indictment with Mr. Trbic, and he received that indictment in a language he understands, and I answered all his questions in relation to that indictment, and he has asked me to inform you today that there's no need to have the indictment read out in court and that he's prepared to enter his plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. O'Sullivan. Mr. Trbic, can you confirm that, as far as you're concerned, it's not necessary for us to read out the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now I have to ask you how you're going to plead on the fourth count of the indictment whereby you are charged with murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You plead not guilty. I'd like to ask the registrar to take note of the fact that the accused has told us that he pleads not guilty on the count against him, a count of crime against humanity. Mr. Trbic, you can sit down. Mr. Trbic, you've just pleaded not guilty. That means that there was -- there will be a pre-trial stage before the actual trial starts. The pre-trial stage is provided for by the Rules, Rule 65 bis (A) of the Rules of the Tribunal. It will be my duty to convene a Status Conference every 120 days. We'll then have the opportunity to meet again and raise, if necessary, a number of issues or discuss problems that might have occurred during these -- this period. The pre-trial stage is aimed at organising exchanges between the parties, between the Defence and the Prosecution, so as to ensure an expeditious preparation for trial, and Status Conferences are also, for me, an opportunity to find out if your detention is going well and if there is any problem. Furthermore, as part of the proceedings under Rule 65 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, any accused may file a motion for provisional release. Pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) I should remind the Prosecutor that he is duty-bound to disclose to the Defence copies of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought. Furthermore, I should also tell you, but your counsel is perfectly aware of that, I shall remind you that in accordance with Rule 72(A), you have 30 days once the Prosecutor has disclosed all of this material, you have 30 days to file any preliminary motion you might like to file. Now I'm going to turn to the Prosecutor to ask him what is the status of disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have the material and are prepared to provide it when Defence would like it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. O'Sullivan, you're the Defence counsel of the accused. May I suppose that you're the permanent counsel of the accused? Can you confirm that for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, I have been assigned as duty counsel for the initial appearance, and it's a matter I'll have to review with both Mr. Trbic and the Registry, in which case, when that's all settled, we'll proceed with receipt of the supporting materials from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Trbic, the counsel here has told me that he's the duty counsel for today's initial appearance. As for the future -- as for future proceedings, do you have a lawyer that you want to assign or that you already know his name, or are you now considering whether you're going to ask for Mr. O'Sullivan to be your Defence counsel? Do you have any information you can provide me about your counsel, counsel who will assist you in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I still haven't made a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Trbic, you've understood that the Prosecutor will only disclose the material once you have finally retained Defence counsel. It's only at that point that the time period will start, time period during which you can file a preliminary motion. But you've just told me that you're still thinking about your Defence counsel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You can sit down. Mr. O'Sullivan, I would like to ask you to keep in touch with Mr. -- with the Registrar and Mr. Trbic for further proceedings in this case. Now, I'd like to turn to the Prosecutor, because I'm also the Pre-Trial Judge in the Pandurevic case and in another case. I would like to know if the Prosecutor has made any progress in its efforts to obtain a joinder of cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I continue to work on that, Your Honour, and it becomes more complicated by events outside the Tribunal, but we'll continue to work and hopefully get that material filed within a reasonable time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But that -- I've had a look at the situation. Currently the Chamber is being seized of the Borovcanin case, Pandurevic, and also the case of Mr. Trbic. Trial Chamber II, with different Judges, has been seized with the case of Miletic, Gvero and Tolimir, but currently Tolimir is at large. There is also the case of Popovic, Vujadin, but no Chamber has been assigned for these cases. There would also be the case of Beara, the Trial Chamber III has been assigned on that case. And there's also the case of Nikolic that was assigned to Trial Chamber I. Have I given a good description of the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I believe you've named them all. I believe Popovic has been assigned to a Chamber, and I'm a little mixed up at this point which one it actually is. The -- we have now, I think, just recently received word that counsel has been assigned to just about everyone, so the work should seriously begin right away. I'm told that Popovic is currently in Trial Chamber III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I wanted to draw the Defence's attention to the fact. Mr. O'Sullivan, I want to draw your attention to the fact, because all these cases might be joined, and we would then have a single case for all these accused. Naturally, that would enable the Tribunal to save precious time. This would be very desirable, but as the Prosecution has pointed out, there are certain issues outside the power of the Tribunal upon which this depends. There's an entire series of factors that have to be taken into consideration. Given the courtrooms available, we cannot put nine accused on trial since we have two or three places at the maximum for the accused, but I know that this is a matter that is currently being considered. At this point in time, Mr. O'Sullivan, is there anything you would like to say, any other issues you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Not at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, before we adjourn, Mr. Trbic, there are a couple of questions I have to put to you. The first question concerns the conditions in the Detention Unit. Do you find them satisfactory? Are you being visited? Have you run into any problems? If -- if you have encountered any problems, inform us of the fact immediately so that I can instruct the Registry to deal with them. But perhaps there are no problems. Could you enlighten me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the conditions are quite satisfactory. I have no problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the second issue that I would like to raise concerns your health. Is everything fine? Do you require medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My health is not very good, but I'm being treated on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The doctor assigned to the Detention Unit is supervising you, and he sees you on a regular basis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. You may sit down now. As I said, the next Status Conference will be held in four months' time. It is May now. So we have June, July, August, and then September. So we will see each other again at the beginning of September. That is quite certain. And at the beginning of September, we should be in a position to be informed of the name of Defence counsel of your choice. The material will have been disclosed to you through your Defence, and your Defence counsel will file any preliminary motions that need to be filed. So, Mr. Trbic, we will now adjourn. And I would like to thank everyone in the courtroom. We will now adjourn. Thank you.
